newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard sets no wake zone on Missouri River.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard sets no wake zone on Missouri River.

text.p: Rising water levels on the Missouri River have prompted the U.S. Coast Guard to set a no wake zone early this week from Waverly, Mo. to St Charles, Mo., just north of St Louis.

"Mariners must use a slow, safe speed to prevent wake damage to levees and property along the river banks" in a no wake zone, said Bob Hildebrand, chief warrant officer, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at St Louis.
He noted the Missouri River from Sioux City, Iowa to St. Charles was at or above flood stage with the exception of Kansas City, Mo.
The high water was attributed to melting snow in the upper Midwest, which is now flowing into rivers.
"The Missouri River at Kansas City stands at 25.3 feet and is slowly rising and flood stage is at 32 feet," Hildebrand said.
The Missouri River at St Charles was cresting on Wednesday at 28.2 feet, 3.2 feet above the 25-foot flood stage, he said.
But he cautioned high water was still flowing down from upriver and water levels at St Charles again, could rise again.
The St Charles County emergency management was monitoring the river levels.
"There is a concern because of the high waters above flood stage but so far, there is no serious threat to flooding of levees," Hildebrand said.
